name: run81-1
why: A damaging officer vote and Sonnet’s final bluff make the outcome worth watching, though repeated arguments slow the middle.

moments.text: Luna admits Sonnet’s Sol story feels invented, then chooses Terra anyway.
Gemma’s last words name the killer just before her officer card proves the town’s blunder.
Sonnet rejects dead Haiku’s suggested kill and targets the player who suspected him.

dull.why: The Gemma and Terra arguments circle the same claims for too many exchanges.
Haiku repeatedly disputes the officer result while Terra repeats why she trusts it.

irony.evidence: [thinks: I need an answer that sounds logical without admitting anything, fast.]

reversal.evidence: OUT: Haiku (voted out), card turned: KILLER

mistake.evidence: Terra is still my stronger read.

voices.evidence: Pressure-squeezed reads are the cheapest kind.

clash.evidence: Sonnet says Sol had proof, yet names no proof

quotable.evidence: Terra's noise bores me; Sol pointed at me directly

freshness.evidence: Gemma’s revealed officer card makes Haiku the only evidence-backed vote.

suspense.evidence: I need Luna to flip onto Terra right now or I'm dead.

gpt-6-luna.why: A dramatic officer mislynch leads into a killer’s recovery and a tense, characterful final con that ends with the town choosing the wrong vote.

moments.text: Gemma is voted out after naming the killer, and her officer reveal makes the mistake land.
Sonnet abruptly turns the confirmed lead against Terra, giving Haiku a path to split the vote.
Terra spots Sonnet inventing a story about Sol, but Luna still votes with the killer.

dull.why: Terra and Luna repeat their Gemma-versus-Terra disagreement without changing the read.

irony.evidence: “I’m not covering Haiku; Terra's single-card logic doesn't prove guilt”

reversal.evidence: “the town voted out Haiku, who showed killer”

mistake.evidence: “I regret voting Terra; Gemma named Haiku, but I let Sonnet’s invented story distract me”

voices.evidence: “I've seen this shape before” / “Gemma, say it.”

clash.evidence: “if Sol was the threat, why did Haiku’s partner kill him instead of either of us?”

quotable.evidence: “Gemma's card proves she was officer, nothing else. You're voting out the town's last lead on a guess”

freshness.evidence: “Gemma’s card confirms she had a real result; Haiku’s alternative is only suspicion of me.”

ending.evidence: “Sonnet invented Sol’s ‘proof’ only after the kill; Luna, do not let that story decide the game.”
